headline: A giant bridge for mountain lions is almost ready

sources.title: World's largest wildlife crossing nears completion in California (Popular Science)
World's largest wildlife crossing is on track to open this winter, unless El Niño intervenes (Los Angeles Times)
Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing to open in December (Spectrum News)

chunks.text: A giant bridge for animals is almost finished over U.S. Highway 101, a busy freeway near Los Angeles. It is the world's largest [[wildlife crossing]]. It is about 210 feet long and stretches across ten [[lanes]] of traffic. Crews have {{put in}} 6,000 [[native plants]] on top. By April 2026, bees, butterflies and a [[lizard]] named Bob had already {{moved in}}. A [[ribbon cutting]] is planned for December 2, 2026.

verbs.correct: To plant something in the ground
verbs.why: Every spring, my dad puts in tomatoes along the back fence. The city puts in new trees on our street each fall. Crews have put in 6,000 native plants on top.

verbs.correct: To start living in a place
verbs.wrong: To visit a place for food
verbs.why: A new family moves in next door almost every summer. Birds move in as soon as we hang a new birdhouse. By April 2026, bees, butterflies and a lizard named Bob had already moved in.

chunks.text: The bridge was built mainly for [[mountain lions]]. Freeways and towns have {{boxed in}} the big cats of the Santa Monica Mountains. The freeway {{cuts them off}} from lions to the north, so many lions [[breed]] with [[close relatives]]. California now lists them as a [[threatened species]]. Computer models show the lions could {{die out}} within 50 years if this starts to harm their ability to have cubs.

verbs.correct: To trap in a small area
verbs.wrong: To mark an area on a map
verbs.why: High fences box in the horses on the farm. New houses box in the deer that live near our town. Freeways and towns have boxed in the big cats of the Santa Monica Mountains.

verbs.wrong: To lead the way for others
verbs.why: Deep snow cuts the mountain village off every winter. A flooded road often cuts the farm off from town. The freeway cuts them off from lions to the north, so many lions breed with close relatives.

Many old languages die out when the last speakers are gone. Some plants die out when the summers get too hot. Computer models show the lions could die out within 50 years if this starts to harm their ability to have cubs.

chunks.text: Heavy rain in the winter of 2022 to 2023 {{pushed back}} the first [[finish date]] of late 2025. In early October 2026, crews still had to move about 3 million [[cubic feet]] of [[soil]]. Forecasters expect a strong El Niño, a weather pattern that can bring heavy rain. Flooding could {{shut down}} the work for [[safety reasons]]. The builders hope to {{wrap up}} the job before big storms arrive. The project costs 114 million dollars. Some [[critics]] have {{spoken out}} against its cost and delays.

verbs.correct: To move to a later date
verbs.why: Bad weather often pushes back the start of the game. My boss pushes back our meeting when she is busy. Heavy rain in the winter of 2022 to 2023 pushed back the first finish date of late 2025.
Heavy snow shuts down the schools for a day or two. A power failure shuts down the whole factory. Flooding could shut down the work for safety reasons.
Painters usually wrap up a small job in two days. I wrap up my homework before dinner. The builders hope to wrap up the job before big storms arrive.

verbs.correct: To say in public what you think
verbs.wrong: To give money to a cause
verbs.why: Many students speak out against the new school rules. Doctors often speak out about the dangers of smoking. Some critics have spoken out against its cost and delays.

chunks.text: Wildlife experts say the bridge will {{open up}} the hills to the north to lions that need [[mates]]. The lions' [[genetic diversity]] should then {{go up}}. By early October 2026, coyotes, deer and a mother lion with two cubs had {{shown up}} on a [[trail camera]] near the bridge. Scientists also found three [[kittens]] in the hills nearby. Once they {{grow up}} and leave their mother, they could be among the first lions to use the bridge.

verbs.correct: To make a place easy to reach
verbs.wrong: To give a place a new name
verbs.why: A new road opens up the north side of the lake to visitors. The new bus line opens up the beach to more families. Wildlife experts say the bridge will open up the hills to the north to lions that need mates.
Rent goes up almost every year in big cities. The number of birds in the park goes up in the spring. The lions' genetic diversity should then go up.

Deer often show up in our backyard at night. My cat shows up at the door when it is hungry. By early October 2026, coyotes, deer and a mother lion with two cubs had shown up on a trail camera near the bridge.
Children grow up very quickly. Most young birds grow up in just a few weeks. Once they grow up and leave their mother, they could be among the first lions to use the bridge.

mainIdea.s: A huge bridge for animals is nearly ready over a busy freeway near Los Angeles. It should help trapped mountain lions reach new mates, which experts say they badly need to survive.
mainIdea.why: Many lions breed with close relatives and could die out. The bridge will open up the hills to the north to lions that need mates.

mainIdea.s: A large bridge over a freeway near Los Angeles will soon be ready for mountain lions. Its main goal is to stop the big cats from entering nearby towns and neighborhoods at night.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the bridge is meant to help the lions reach other lions. The freeway cuts them off, so many breed with close relatives.

mainIdea.s: A new study says bright city lights keep big cats awake at night near Los Angeles. The scientists want darker streets close to the hills where these animals live and hunt.
mainIdea.why: This is about a giant bridge for animals over a freeway. It should help boxed in mountain lions reach other lions.

tf.s: The bridge was built mainly to help mountain lions.
tf.why: Freeways and towns have boxed in the big cats, so they need a safe way to reach other lions.

tf.s: The lions can easily reach other lions in the hills to the north.
tf.why: The ten-lane freeway cuts them off from those lions, so many breed with close relatives.

tf.s: Heavy rain pushed back the bridge's first finish date.
tf.why: Rain in the winter of 2022 to 2023 pushed back the first finish date of late 2025. A ribbon cutting is now planned for December 2, 2026.

tf.s: The bridge is already open to wild animals.
tf.why: It is almost finished, and the builders hope to wrap up the job before big storms arrive.

tf.s: No one has spoken out against the cost of the bridge.
tf.why: Some critics have spoken out against the project's cost and its delays.

tf.s: A mother lion with cubs has shown up on a camera near the bridge.
tf.why: A trail camera near the bridge caught her and her two cubs, along with coyotes and deer.

lines.text: Did you hear about the giant bridge for animals near Los Angeles?
The one over the freeway? I thought it was already finished.
Almost. It should open on December 2, 2026. Heavy rain {{pushed back}} the first date by about a year.
Well, if it helps the animals, it's [[worth the wait]].
That's the idea. The mountain lions there are {{boxed in}} by freeways and towns.
So the freeway {{cuts them off}} from other lions?
Exactly. So many of them have cubs with close relatives.
That can't be good for them.
It isn't. Computer models show they could {{die out}} within 50 years.
Wow. So there's [[a lot riding on]] this bridge.
There really is. Crews have {{put in}} thousands of native plants on top.
Are any animals coming close to it yet?
Coyotes, deer and a mother lion with two cubs have {{shown up}} on a camera near it.
[[So far, so good]], then. How much does it cost?
It's 114 million dollars, and some critics have {{spoken out}} against it.
That's a lot of money. But for the lions, it could be [[a game changer]].
I agree. The first finish date was late 2025, so this has been [[a long time coming]].
Let's hope the builders {{wrap up}} before the big storms arrive.
